target_customer: Underserved Mexican consumers and micro-businesses needing small digital credit lines
problem: Many Mexicans lack access to affordable small credit and need a lender that builds their financial health.
business_model: Consumer lending with interest and fees

founders.name: Debashish Bhadra
founders.background_notes: YC page: Head of Credit at Konfio, senior credit manager at Capital One.

founders.name: Gianfranco Gentille
founders.background_notes: YC page lists operations, strategy, product and finance roles.

competitors.name: Kueski
competitors.what: Digital short-term loans and BNPL in Mexico
competitors.funding_then: Series D $102M reported, date not given

competitors.name: Baubap
competitors.what: AI micro-lender in Mexico with loans from MX$500 to MX$5,000

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit scoring and a lending app are standard for fintech lenders; the challenge is underwriting data and funding.

defensibility.rationale: Lending is a crowded market with funded rivals. Underwriting data improves with repayment history but competitors had similar advantages.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals kept raising capital; BelozFi stayed active with its app listed at 4.8 stars from 6.8k ratings.

market_need_then: Large unbanked and underbanked population in Mexico and rapid growth of digital microloans, per rival traction.

branding.domain_note: Uses belozfi.com.mx. Parent entity appears as amiloz on YC jobs and Google Play.

identity.voice_and_tone: Financial health focused, interest-free first loan marketing

branding.community_and_virality: App Store rating of 4.8 from 6.8k ratings

brand_strength.rationale: App ratings show usage, but no press or brand story and the name varies between Beloz, BelozFi and amiloz.

outcome_analysis: BelozFi is active with about 29 staff in Mexico City and a well-rated lending app. Founders came from Capital One, Konfio and DiDi, which fits credit underwriting. Funding is thinly documented in aggregators, so the scale of capital behind the loan book is unknown. It competes with larger funded lenders, and no failure or exit signal was found.
notes: Funding unverified and conflicting across aggregators: Dealroom $125K seed (no date), Briter $300K seed dated 2025-01-30, Caplight total $1.75M, Extruct Latitud seed dated 2023-01-01. Not recorded as rounds. The company site returned 403. Founder education not found. Kueski date is from a March 2022 snippet via CB Insights page; Baubap source is about ten months after the batch start. YC page names Latitud as backer without amounts. No outcome news found. Completeness pass: Both recorded rounds rest on a single database each (Caplight for the 2025-02-15 early round, Extruct for the Latitud seed). Caplight reports total funding of 1.75M, larger than the amounts recorded, so a gap is known. Dealroom 125K seed and Briter 300K seed (2025-01-30) were not recorded: the Briter figure could not be re-found.
